messages:
rachael: Heads-up — during int8 bringup for the new 30B fork I hit a reproducible divergence that looks specific to a late-binding prefill path. Repro steps + logs attached.

rachael: Repro command i used:
```
python infra/tests/prefill_repro.py --model magnet30b-v2 --quant int8 --prefill-mode late-binding --seq 16384 --seed 42
```

rachael: Failure: model outputs match until ~8k tokens, then token probabilities shift and sampled outputs diverge. Not just sampling noise — deterministic top-k mismatch.

dmitri: can you attach the minimal trace? also which kernel (fused/planar) and rotary scaling params?

rachael: trace: s3://redwood-ci/repro/3180009999/repro.tar.gz (contains kv-dump after prefill, logits diff, and a tiny harness). kernel=rocm-fused-2, pos_scale=default (no manual override).

sam: quick hypothesis: late-binding means we insert KV frames after streaming started; if the RoPE phase offset is computed relative to a different absolute position the kv indices could be misaligned. did you try forcing synchronous prefill (no late-binding)?

rachael: yes — forcing sync prefill (prefill-mode=sync) removes divergence entirely. latency increases ~35% but correctness is back.

kevin: interesting — so it's not quantization alone. Could be ordering of kv writes vs. rotary index calculation when using packed int8 layout. Have you inspected kv keys at the boundary?

rachael: pasted small excerpt from kv dump near boundary (token index ~8192):
```
# kv_key[8190..8195]
8190: 0x3fa4b1c2 0x... (float-ish pattern)
8191: 0x3fa4b2d0 0x...
8192: 0x0000ffff 0x... <-- looks like padding inserted
8193: 0x3fa4b300 0x...
```

rachael: That 0x0000ffff looks like a sentinel we use for 'late insert placeholder' in the int8 packing path.

sam: ugh. packing layer uses a flat memcpy that assumes contiguous physical layout. Late inserts + placeholder semantics could shift subsequent KV positions by 1 element which then shifts RoPE phase alignment for all later tokens.

dmitri: can we reproduce with an unquantized run but replicating the placeholder behavior? i.e., inject a sentinel in float32 packing to see if rotor shift happens.

rachael: ran that — float32 + placeholder yields the same divergence pattern. So root cause looks to be index/addressing, not quantization rounding.

kevin: good find. Two followups: 1) we need an immediate mitigation for hosted to avoid regressions (disable late-binding on affected configs), 2) we should add an assert in the packer that forbids placeholders shifting downstream indexes.

ci-bot: CI results for repro (3180009999) — baseline(sync) vs late-binding:
- token-mismatch-rate @8k+ : baseline=0.002%, late-binding=0.58%
- mean logit delta (L1) after 8k: 0.0008 vs 0.034
- perf: baseline 1.0x, late-binding 1.35x (faster)

dmitri: those numbers look convincing. I can open a patch to change the packer to use an explicit slot-reservation API instead of ad-hoc memcpy. Will need reviews from runtime and quant.

rachael: created a tiny repro test in tests/eng/kvcache/test_late_binding_shift.py and added it to the longcontext smoke. see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123

kevin: for the model-onboard checklist we should add: full longprefill smoke with late-binding enabled (expect identical outputs to sync), plus a post-quantization kv-index integrity check (hash of keys after prefill).

sam: also add a diag that dumps 'kv_index_map' with absolute offsets to logs when debug enabled. That would make future bisects faster.

rachael: agreed. Action items:
- dmitri: packer refactor PR + tests (owner)
- kev: add runtime flag to disable late-binding for affected instance types (owner: kevin)
- sam: add kv_index_map logger and CI gate for longprefill (owner)
- rachael: coordinate canary with hosting (small cohort) once PRs land

kevin: timeline?

dmitri: targeting EOD tomorrow for initial packer PR, then 24h for reviews.

rachael: I'll schedule a brief canary run after merges. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: nightly longprefill smoke (post-PR) queued for 3180070000.
